newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast gasoline falls with weak demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast gasoline falls with weak demand.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices fell late Thursday, as fading demand left refiners with more supply and squeezed their margins, traders said.
"No one's enthusiastic to buy barrels," one trader said.
U.S. Department of Energy reported Wednesday that total supply held in the region's refiners rose about 100,000 barrels last week, leaving stocks 29.3 million barrels.
Meanwhile, retail prices for regular unleaded gasoline, a key component of margins, fell about 2.4 cents last week in western states.
Overall, analysts say margins are 21 percent weaker than last quarter
Los Angeles traders saw bids for CARB-grade regular gasoline fall two cents from Wednesday to 61 cents a gallon, amid light buying.

Premium grade CARB saw its advantage over conventional slip to three cents. The price has fallen because wintertime vapor pressure additives have enlarged the gasoline pool some five to 15 percent, traders said.
L.A. conventional grade fell a cent to 58/59 cents a gallon.
L.A. low sulphur diesel and jet fuel flattened out at 66/67 cents a gallon early, after getting a slight boost from NYMEX heating oil prices Wednesday.
CARB-grade diesel in L.A. remained 76/77 cents a gallon. Its San Francisco counterpart has fallen to five cents under recently, with agricultural demand fading in Northern California.
